ety.text: Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *खोव (khova) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-) of uncertain further origin. Perhaps from Sanskrit क्षोद (kṣoda), whence the lemma below. Compare Punjabi ਖੋਆ (khoā), Nepali खुवा (khuwā), Marathi खोवा (khovā), खवा (khavā), and Bengali খোয়া (khōẇa).

Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *kes- Proto-Indo-European *ksew-? Proto-Indo-European *k⁽ʷ⁾sewd- Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšawd- Sanskrit क्षुद् (kṣud) Sanskrit क्षोद (kṣoda) Prakrit खोय (khoya) Hindi खोआ Inherited from Prakrit खोय (khoya) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-), from older खोद (khoda) from Sanskrit क्षोद (kṣoda), from the root क्षुद् (kṣud, “to crush”).

ety.text: From चक्कर (cakkar) + -आना (-ānā).
Inherited from Prakrit चट्टेइ (caṭṭei, “to devour with relish, eat noisily”, onomatopoeia). Compare Gujarati ચાટવું (cāṭvũ), Marathi चाटणे (ċāṭṇe), Bengali চাটা (caṭa).

ety.text: From चोला (colā) + -ई (-ī).

Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit *चउड (caüḍa). Beyond that, it is possibly from Sanskrit चतुर् (catur, “four”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀟- (-ḍa-). Compare the semantically parallel Sanskrit चतुष्क (catuṣka, “made of four; courtyard”), whence Hindi चौक (cauk). Many of the New Indo-Aryan languages retain the "flat area" meaning. Cognate with Punjabi ਚੌੜਾ (cauṛā), Nepali चौडा (cauḍā), Gujarati ચોડું (coḍũ), Assamese চৌৰা (soura), Bengali চওড়া (coōṛa), Odia ଚଉଡ଼ା (cauṛā).
Borrowed from Classical Persian زَرْدِی (zardī, “yellowness”), from زَرْد (zard, “yellow”). By surface analysis, ज़र्द (zard) + -ई (-ī). Related to ज़र (zar) and हरा (harā).
From तटस्थ (taṭasth, “neutral”) + -ईकरण (-īkaraṇ, “-isation”).

x: प्रधानाचार्य महोदय लगभग पिताजी के सम[-]आयु थे। उन्होंने अपने सिर के बंजर वन को एक टोपी से ढक रखा था। तोंदीला बदन और बात-बात पर हँसने की उनकी आदत।

ety.text: Inherited from Prakrit तुंदिल्ल (tuṃdilla), तुंदिल (tuṃdila), from Sanskrit तुन्दिल (tundila). By surface analysis, तोंद (tond, “pot-belly”) + -ईला (-īlā).

ety.text: Deverbal form of दमकना (damaknā).

Hindi verb set दौड़ना (dauṛnā) दौड़ाना (dauṛānā) दौड़वाना (dauṛvānā) From Proto-New Indo-Aryan *दवडइ (davaḍaï), an extended form of दवइ (davaï, “to go away”) with Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀟- (-ḍa-), from Sanskrit द्रवति (drávati). Cognate with Punjabi ਦੌੜਣਾ (dauṛṇā) / دَوڑنا (dauṛṇā), Sindhi ڊوڙَڻُ (ḍoṛaṇu) / डोड़णु (ḍoṛaṇu), Gujarati દોડવું (doḍvũ), Nepali दौडनु (dauḍanu), Marathi दौडणे (dauḍṇe), Assamese দৌৰা (doura), Bengali দৌড়ানো (dōuṛanō). Through the Sanskrit root द्रु (dru, “to run, melt”), related to Hindi द्रुत (drut, “quick”).
From धमार (dhamār).

From नाभिकीय (nābhikīya, “nuclear”) + भौतिकी (bhautikī, “physics”).

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian بابل (bāḇil), from Arabic بَابِل (bābil), from Aramaic בבל (bāḇel), from Akkadian 𒆍𒀭𒊏𒆠 (Bābilim).
Borrowed from Classical Persian بَارِش (bāriš). Despite similar pronunciation and existence of Indic-Iranic doublets for other pairs of terms, probably unrelated to Hindi वर्षा (varṣā, “rain”).
Inherited from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀯𑀺𑀘𑁆𑀙𑀼𑀅 (vicchua), from Sanskrit वृश्चिक (vṛścika). Cognate to Marathi विंचू (viñcū). Doublet of वृश्चिक (vŕścik), a tatsama.

ety.text: From Prakrit *सण्णाएइ (saṇṇāei), from Sanskrit संनादयति (saṃnādayati), from the root नद् (nad, “to resound”). Turner supposes that the irregular retention of geminate -nn- is expressive onomatopoeic, while it could also be semi-learned—compare संनाद (sannād, “consonance”).

ety.text: Inherited from Old Hindi समझना (samajhanā), समुझना (samujhanā), from Prakrit संबुज्झइ (saṃbujjhaï), संबुज्झदि (saṃbujjhadi), from Sanskrit सम्बुध्यते (sambudhyate). Cognate with Punjabi ਸਮਝਣਾ (samjhaṇā) / سَمجھݨا (samjhṇā), Gujarati સમજવું (samajvũ), Marathi समजणे (samajṇe). Compare now-archaic बूझना (būjhnā), derived from the same verb without a prefix.
